items.title: Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Shri Jitin Prasada Visits Poland to Strengthen Bilateral Trade, Investment and Technology Cooperation
items.summary: The visit followed the recent visit of Polish Prime Minister, Mr. Donald Tusk to India last month and reflected the growing momentum in bilateral engagement between the two countries. The continued high-level political exchanges in 2026 underline the strengthening of the India–Poland Strategic Partnership, established in 2024 during the landmark visit of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to Poland.

facts.text: The discussions focused on expanding bilateral cooperation in emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), semiconductors, data centres and cybersecurity.

In his meeting with the Secretary of State in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Poland, Mr. Ignacy Niemczycki, Shri Prasada held extensive discussions on opportunities emerging from the India–European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA), which will come into effect in the coming months.

He also highlighted the opportunities expected to emerge from the India–EU Free Trade Agreement and encouraged businesses from both countries to leverage the agreement to expand market access, strengthen trade and investment ties and explore new avenues for cooperation.

items.title: Indian Railways Registers Freight Loading of 145.07 Million Tonnes in October 2026
items.summary: Higher freight loading and increased freight earnings reflect Indian Railways’ efforts towards supporting economic growth and strengthening the country’s logistics sector. Indian Railways achieved its highest-ever freight loading for October, transporting 145.07 million tonnes of freight during the month, compared to 133.93 million tonnes in October 2025, registering a growth of 8.32 per cent.

facts.text: Indian Railways achieved its highest-ever freight loading for October, transporting 145.07 million tonnes of freight during the month, compared to 133.93 million tonnes in October 2025, registering a growth of 8.32 per cent.

Food Grains loading increased by 26.3 per cent, Domestic Coal by 16.0 per cent, Balance Other Goods by 11.0 per cent, Clinker by 10.4 per cent, Domestic Containers by 6.3 per cent, Iron Ore by 5.0 per cent, Mineral Oil by 1.9 per cent and Finished Steel by 0.5 per cent.

To meet the increased requirement of power houses, Indian Railways stepped up domestic coal transportation, supplying an average of 469.8 rakes per day during October 2026, compared to 393.2 rakes per day in the corresponding month last year, registering a growth of 19.5 per cent.
The strong performance in October 2026 builds upon the growth recorded during the first seven months of FY 2026-27 (April–October).
